summary: Interfaces is strategically sound but still not execution-ready. The 2026-03-15 PLAN.md update added meaningful new scope: an as-code contract pack between Lyra OS and PXS. This is a material change that elevates Priority 2 and was reflected in a TOP_PRIORITIES refresh. Two structural blockers remain open from yesterday: broken assembly metadata links and no closed-loop downstream verification evidence. The as-code rollout adds surface area that compounds the verification gap if not addressed concurrently.

materialChanges.detail: PLAN.md updated on 2026-03-15 (commit a33ac35) to add objective 4: Define the shared As-Code Contract Pack between Lyra OS and PXS, with sub-focus on shared schemas, shared enums/taxonomy, and PXS execution object mapping. This is a meaningful scope expansion within Priority 2 that was not yet reflected in TOP_PRIORITIES.

topPriorities.title: Resolve Interfaces identity, scope, and ownership boundaries
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Strategic guardrail. Charter is narrowed and documented; requires ongoing enforcement particularly as new as-code scope is added to the plan.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Keep ownership stance explicit — especially as provider-specific vs. cross-cutting contract surfaces are distinguished in the as-code rollout.

topPriorities.title: Make the Interfaces assembly real, self-consistent, and consumable — including as-code contract pack
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Assembly has known broken metadata links. As-code rollout is newly added to the plan but not yet started. Both must be resolved before Priority 3 can close.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: (a) Correct assembly.yaml metadata links; (b) scope the minimal shared As-Code Contract Pack surface between Lyra OS and PXS.

topPriorities.title: Run one downstream consumption pilot with evidence and one preventive drift guard
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Evidence path is not closed. VERIFY contains unchecked criteria; no linked workflow evidence is surfaced. As-code rollout adds new surface that requires verification discipline.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Require one real workflow evidence link in VERIFY; enforce changelog-plus-verification drift guard for meaningful contract changes.

blockers.title: Assembly metadata/documentation path inconsistency — unresolved from yesterday
blockers.detail: assembly.yaml links changelog/activation/verify to missing `assemblies/interfaces/v0.1/*` paths; real files live at `assemblies/prompting-and-3pp/v0.1/*`. This weakens installability and auditability and is a direct blocker for Priority 2.

blockers.title: No closed-loop downstream verification evidence — unresolved from yesterday
blockers.detail: VERIFY.md defines the required evidence but no completed workflow evidence link or pass outcome exists in the reviewed stack. Priority 3 cannot be called done without this.

blockers.title: As-code contract pack not yet started
blockers.detail: PLAN.md now includes defining the shared As-Code Contract Pack between Lyra OS and PXS, but no artifact, scoping work, or execution evidence exists for this objective. This is newly introduced scope as of 2026-03-15.

risksOrOpportunities.title: As-code rollout expands the verification surface prematurely
risksOrOpportunities.detail: Adding as-code contract scope (schemas, enums, PXS object mapping) before the assembly metadata blocker is fixed and before one downstream verification pass exists risks compounding the current evidence gap.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Assembly packaging is not self-consistent
risksOrOpportunities.detail: Broken assembly links are persistent (now 2 days old). Every day without correction weakens the assembly as a real export surface and undermines migration readiness.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Promotion gate remains too thin
risksOrOpportunities.detail: Without one real downstream workflow and linked verification evidence, the product cannot demonstrate behavioral value or control drift credibly.

risksOrOpportunities.title: As-code rollout alignment opportunity
risksOrOpportunities.detail: The plan update to include as-code contract pack work aligns Interfaces with the broader OS-wide as-code direction (also reflected in Delivery and Security plans in the same commit). If executed, this could make Interfaces a genuine enabler for reliable cross-repo exchange rather than just a policy/packaging product.

researchDelta: No new product-local research in this run. The 2026-03-14 research artifact (IMPLEMENT_NOW_FROM_RESEARCH_2026-03-14.md) remains the last formal research input. Material new input is the 2026-03-15 PLAN.md update adding as-code rollout focus.

proposedTdeActions.title: Fix assembly.yaml broken documentation links — this is a quick and concrete unblock
proposedTdeActions.why: Same blocker as yesterday. Correct the three broken link paths. This is a sub-30-minute execution task that would unblock assembly auditability and Priority 2.

proposedTdeActions.title: Scope the minimal As-Code Contract Pack surface before building it
proposedTdeActions.why: PLAN.md now requires this objective. Scoping first keeps the contract surface minimal and prevents premature expansion. Identify the shortest path: one shared schema fragment or enum as a starting point.

proposedTdeActions.title: Close the downstream verification evidence loop
proposedTdeActions.why: Priority 3 is blocked by missing evidence. Identify one real workflow, record evidence link, achieve a VERIFY PASS or PARTIAL outcome. This is the key product value demonstration.
